terms.meaning: A comparison of two quantities by division, written a : b. a and b are its terms.
A ratio whose terms have no common factor except 1. 12 : 18 in simplest form is 2 : 3.
Two ratios that are equal, written a : b :: c : d.
The old Indian method for finding the fourth quantity in a proportion from the other three.

items.name: Making a ratio simple
items.formula: Divide both terms by their HCF
items.example: 24 : 36. The HCF is 12, so the ratio is 2 : 3.

items.name: Equal ratios
items.formula: Multiply both terms by the same number

items.name: Resizing without changing the shape
items.formula: Multiply width and height by the same factor
items.example: A 30 by 20 picture made 2 times bigger is 60 by 40. The ratio stays 3 : 2.

items.name: Finding a missing term
items.formula: a : b :: c : d means a × d = b × c

items.name: Units in a proportion
items.formula: Change to the same unit first

items.name: Dividing a quantity in the ratio m : n
items.formula: Shares are m/(m + n) and n/(m + n) of the total
items.example: ₹700 in the ratio 4 : 3: 700 ÷ 7 = 100, so the shares are ₹400 and ₹300.

items.name: Sharing a profit
items.formula: Share it in the ratio of the money invested
items.example: Investments ₹2000 and ₹3000 give the ratio 2 : 3. A profit of ₹500 becomes ₹200 and ₹300.

mistakes.text: Adding the same number to both terms changes the ratio. 2 : 3 is not 4 : 5.
Age ratios change over time, because both ages increase by the same number. Ages 5 and 10 are 1 : 2, but after 5 years they are 10 : 15, which is 2 : 3.
The order of the terms matters. 3 : 2 is not the same as 2 : 3.
When sharing in the ratio 4 : 3, divide by 7, not by 4 or 3. Add the terms first.
